title: Change a full bin for an empty one under a running machine's discharge chute, between two falling parts
instruction: The machine drops a finished part down its chute into the bin under it every few seconds, and it doesn't stop. A bin takes a lot of exactly 6 parts: once the bin under the chute holds 6, put it on the grey FULL mark and put the empty bin under the chute. Every part must land in a bin.
context: Machines that discharge finished parts one at a time (cut-off saws, presses, moulding machines) fill a bin under their chute, and the operator changes it for an empty one while the machine keeps running: a bin changed late mixes two lots, one changed early leaves a short lot, and a part falling between bins lands on the floor. Hand packers alone are over half a million US workers (BLS OEWS, SOC 53-7064). Here the robot counts the parts as they fall and, after exactly the sixth, completes the change in the 1.8 to 2.4 s before the seventh. Counting is the easy half; the hard half is physical: two 13 cm bins trade places under one point without tipping parts out of the full one or putting a gripper in the next part's path. Taking the full bin away and then fetching the empty one is too slow, so the change has to be one movement. Three lots fall at different times and paces from the same picture, so a change timed on a clock fits only one.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Machine: a grey-green cabinet (28 x 36 cm, 52 cm tall) at the far end of the table, centred at (0.74, 0.00), with a green RUN lamp on its front. From its front, 43 cm up, a yellow open chute (5 cm wide, 3 cm side walls) runs down toward the robot to the top of a yellow drop tube (4.4 cm across, 14 cm long) standing vertically over (0.34, 0.00), its mouth 19 cm above the table. Parts: ten zinc-plated steel bushings (25 mm across, 20 mm long, 55 g), all inside the machine at the start; part k (k = 1..10) falls out of the tube's mouth at 0.5 m/s at the lot's time: lot A from 3.5 s every 2.0 s, lot B from 4.6 s every 2.4 s, lot C from 3.0 s every 1.8 s (trial k of a run uses lot k mod 3, lot A first). Two identical blue polypropylene bins (13.2 x 13.2 cm, 7 cm tall; 12 x 12 cm inside; 6 mm walls and floor; 150 g), each with a handle tab (3 cm wide, 12 mm thick) rising 5 cm above the middle of each end wall (its left and right walls): the first, empty, centred at (0.34, 0.00) under the tube; the second, empty, at (0.22, 0.24). FULL mark: a square of dark grey tape (8 mm wide), 17 x 17 cm inside, centred at (0.22, -0.24). Both arms start in the ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: A part is caught by a bin once its centre has been inside that bin (within its 12 x 12 cm inner outline, between its floor and its rim) for 0.3 s in a row. Violation (score 0, latched): a part not caught by a bin within 1.5 s of leaving the tube (on the table, on a rim, in a gripper or off the table), or a caught part out of its bin (over 1 cm outside its inner outline or over 3 cm above its rim) for 0.25 s or more, or a bin fallen off the table (underside 5 cm or more below the table top). The parts must split as the job needs: parts 1 to n caught by the first bin and every later part that has left the tube caught by the second, at least one; any other split scores 0. Placed: the first bin with its centre inside the FULL mark's inner square; the second bin with its centre within 3 cm of (0.34, 0.00); each standing on the table (underside within 1 cm of it, tilted under 10 degrees); a bin still held counts. Score: 0.5 for the first bin placed plus 0.5 for the second placed when n = 6; 0.25 each when n = 5 or 7; 0 for any other n. Success (1.0): n = 6 with both bins placed, held for 1 s; the trial then ends (1.4 s after the seventh part leaves the tube at the earliest). Otherwise the trial runs its 1,200 steps and scores the state at the end; a violation does not end it, but its 0 stands. Doing nothing scores 0 (all parts go into the first bin, which never reaches the mark), and so does waiting for the line to run out (n = 10). Each trial is scored on its own; a run of three trials (lots A, B and C) is scored by their mean. In a real trial, which bin each part falls into is judged from an overhead video, and the placements with a tape measure.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (1 minute at 20 Hz) per trial; three trials (--epochs 3), one per lot
reset_notes: Empty both bins; put the first under the tube and the second on its start mark; collect the ten bushings. A helper behind the machine, out of the arms' reach, drops the bushings into a closed chute that ends in the drop tube, on the lot's beat less the chute's travel time, measured once from a video (a metronome or phone timer: lot A from 3.5 s every 2.0 s, lot B from 4.6 s every 2.4 s, lot C from 3.0 s every 1.8 s).
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The machine is a fixed cabinet; the chute and drop tube are drawn but not solid in the simulation (nothing needs to go near them), and each part appears at the tube's mouth already falling at 0.5 m/s, lying on its side and tumbling slightly differently each time, as a part leaving a tube does. The bushings collide as solid cylinders (a real bushing has a bore). The bins are single rigid bodies with their handle tabs.
scores: Dream-1: 0 in each of lots A, B and C (mean 0; it moved the bins but never changed them between parts 6 and 7). Demo (counts the parts from the top camera): 1.0 in each of A, B and C. Controls: one bin after the other 0; a swap on lot A's clock 1.0 in A, 0 in B and C; doing nothing 0.
